cohort: The study included 45,540 pregnant females aged 18-45, with 22,770 having thalassemia trait and 22,770 without any thalassemia diagnosis, after propensity score matching.
finding: Thalassemia trait in pregnancy was associated with significantly higher risks of anemia, blood transfusion, preeclampsia/eclampsia, cesarean delivery, preterm delivery, intrauterine growth restriction, venous thromboembolism, and intrauterine fetal demise.
mod_finding: Thalassemia trait was associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery (RR: 1.43).
